candidates: When adding a new feature flag to the `StorybookConfigRaw` features interface (in `code/core/src/types/modules/core-common.ts`), choose user-facing, discoverable names rather than internal technical jargon. Avoid terms like 'widget' or overly narrow technical labels. Prefer terminology users are likely to search for in documentation (e.g., 'onboarding') and include a surface-area scope prefix (e.g., 'sidebar') when the flag controls behaviour in a specific part of the UI. The flag name, its default in the preset (`common-preset.ts`), and all usage sites must all use the same identifier.

When reading a feature flag from `global.FEATURES` inside manager components (e.g., `Sidebar.tsx`, `GuidePage.tsx`), always use optional chaining together with a `!== false` guard — `global.FEATURES?.flagName !== false` — so that the flag defaults to its enabled state (`true`) when `FEATURES` is undefined, which can occur in tests and stories.
